primitives.name: Ball Possession Interval
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question What minimal agent-based dynamics explain the statistics of ball-possession intervals (BPIs) in soccer — possession time, pass length, number of passes — and can the model's dynamics be mapped onto a well-understood physical process (Wiener process with drift and an absorbing barrier)?
primitives.assumptions: ['Exponential step lengths (memoryless)', 'Constant pass probability', 'Defender strategy: always head toward ball', 'Neglect field geometry']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T > 60s or Δr exceeds field boundaries

layer2.mapping: BPIs follow a Wiener process with drift μ and diffusion σ, where μ = -0.07 matches empirical drift and σ = 0.39 captures variability in possession duration.
layer2.telemetry: Distribution of T, Δr, and N compared via Jensen–Shannon divergence

primitives.name: Agent-Based Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Three-agent minimalist simulator: two teammates + one defender, discrete time steps Δt=1, 2D motion.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p': 'pass attempt probability (dimensionless)', 'a': 'action radius scale (meters)', 'R1': 'inner radius (meters)', 'R2': 'outer radius (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: ['Discrete time steps Δt = 1', 'Two teammates and one defender', 'Motion in 2D space', 'Free player and defender always accept moves']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When agent positions violate boundary conditions or exceed action radii

layer2.mapping: Simulates BPIs through stochastic agent interactions, producing empirical distributions that mirror real-world possession patterns.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical distribution of BPIs matched against observed data using JS divergence

primitives.name: Possession Transition Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pass attempted with probability p if the defender's action radius does not intercept the teammate-to-teammate line.
primitives.assumptions: ['Passes occur only when defender does not block line of sight', 'Pass probability is fixed across simulations', 'Agents act independently']
primitives.breakdown_regime: When defender's action radius fully encompasses the pass trajectory

layer2.mapping: Models possession transitions as binary outcomes governed by conditional probability, analogous to quantum measurement collapse in probabilistic systems.
layer2.telemetry: Transition frequency between teams validated against match-level data
